title: Street Art and Murals
summary: How cities invite artists to plan and paint huge murals on blank walls, turning quiet streets in places like Riyadh and Jeddah into colorful public landmarks.
poll: Painting a big, colorful mural is a good way to use a blank city wall.

versions.title: Street Art: Big Pictures on Walls
versions.text:
A mural is big. It is a painting on a wall. It is outside. You can see it.

Schools have murals. Shops have murals. Tall buildings have murals too. A mural is part of the wall.

The word mural means wall. It is an old word. People have used paint on walls for a long time.

A city can ask an artist. The artist can paint a wall. The wall starts blank. The artist must ask first.

A small plan must get big. Artists use a grid. It is like boxes. This helps make the plan big on the wall.

Painting takes a team. It can take many days. In Riyadh, walls get bright. In Jeddah, walls get bright too. People like the bright colors.

versions.title: Street Art: Big Pictures on Walls
versions.text:
A mural is a big painting. It is made on a wall. It is usually outside, so many people can see it.

Murals are found on schools and shops. They are also on tall buildings. A mural is part of the wall, not a frame.

The word mural comes from an old word for wall. People have put paint on walls for a long time. This kind of art is now called street art.

First, an artist gets asked. A city or shop owner asks the artist. The wall starts out blank. The artist must also ask for permission.

A small plan must become big. Artists draw a grid on the plan. It is like a set of boxes. They draw a matching grid on the wall. Each box helps copy the plan at the right size.

Making a mural takes a team. It is rarely just one person. It can take many days. In Riyadh and Jeddah, walls that were once blank and gray now show bright colors.

versions.title: Street Art and Murals
versions.text:
A mural is a large painting. It is made right on a wall. It is usually outside. Many people walk by and see it.

Murals can be found on schools, shops, and tall buildings. Unlike a painting in a frame, a mural is part of the building itself.

The word mural comes from an old word, murus. It means wall. People have put paint on walls for a very long time. Today, this kind of art is often called street art.

First, an artist must be asked. A city or a building owner asks the artist to paint a wall. The wall starts out blank. The town can pick a theme. It could be local history or nature. The artist must get a yes first.

Turning a small sketch into a huge mural takes care. Artists draw a grid over the small plan. They draw a matching, bigger grid on the wall. Each square can then be copied at the right size. For tall walls, artists use a lift.

Making a mural is rarely a one-person job. A whole team of artists often works together. It can take many days. In Riyadh and Jeddah, murals have begun to brighten walls, turning plain, gray walls into bright colors.

versions.title: Street Art and Murals
versions.text:
A mural is a large painting. It is made right on a wall. The person who paints one is an artist too.

Murals can be found on schools, shops, bridges, and tall buildings. Unlike a painting that hangs in a frame, a mural becomes a lasting part of the wall itself.

The word mural comes from an old word, murus, which means wall. People have put paint on walls for thousands of years. Today, this kind of art is often called street art.

Before an artist can paint a big mural, a city, a school, or an owner must first ask the artist. The wall usually starts out blank. The town may pick a theme, such as local history or nature. The artist must get a yes before painting a wall that is not theirs.

Turning a small sketch into a giant mural takes care. Artists draw a grid over the small plan. Then they draw a matching, much bigger grid on the wall. Each square can be copied at the right size. For very tall walls, artists use a lift to reach high up safely.

Making a mural is rarely a one-person job. A whole team of artists often works together. Sometimes people from the town help paint parts too. In Riyadh and Jeddah, murals have begun to brighten walls that were once blank and gray. Quiet streets are now turning bright and colorful.

versions.title: Street Art and Murals
versions.text:
A mural is a large painting made directly on a wall, usually outdoors. The person who paints one is called a muralist.

Murals appear on the sides of schools, shops, bridges, and tall buildings. Unlike a painting that hangs in a frame, a mural becomes a lasting part of the wall itself.

The word mural comes from an old Latin word, murus, meaning wall. People have put paint on walls for thousands of years. Today, this kind of art is often called street art. It has become common in cities everywhere.

Before an artist can paint a big mural, a city or a building owner usually asks the artist first. They offer a blank wall to use. The community often picks a theme, such as local history or nature. The artist must get official permission. Painting a wall that is not theirs is against the rules.

Turning a small sketch into a giant mural takes careful planning, since the design must be scaled to fit the wall. Artists draw a grid over the small design. They draw a matching, much bigger grid on the wall. Every square can then be copied at the right size. For very tall walls, artists use scaffolding or a lift to reach high places safely.

Painting a mural is rarely a one-person job. Large murals often need a whole team of artists working together. Sometimes people from the town help paint smaller parts too. In Saudi cities such as Riyadh and Jeddah, murals have begun to brighten walls that were once blank and gray.

versions.title: Street Art and Murals
versions.text:
A mural is a large-scale painting executed directly on a wall, usually outdoors. The person who paints one is known as a muralist. Murals transform plain, ordinary walls into vibrant works of public art that anyone walking by can enjoy.

Murals appear on the sides of schools, shops, bridges, and apartment buildings across cities worldwide. Unlike a painting that hangs inside a frame, a mural becomes a lasting part of the building itself.

The word mural derives from an old Latin word, murus, meaning wall. People have decorated walls with pictures for thousands of years. The large, public murals recognized today are often called street art. They have become far more common over recent decades, especially as cities began holding mural festivals and inviting artists from abroad to collaborate with local talent.

Before an artist can paint a large mural, a city or a building owner usually commissions the artist and offers a blank wall as a canvas. The surrounding community often suggests a theme, such as local history, nature, or a neighborhood story. The artist must obtain official permission, because painting on a wall that belongs to someone else without asking is against the rules, however talented the artist may be.

Turning a small sketch into a giant mural requires careful planning, since the design must be scaled up to the size of a building. Artists often draw a grid over their small design and a matching, much larger grid on the wall, so every square can be copied at the correct scale; some artists now project the design onto the wall at night instead. For very tall walls, artists rely on scaffolding or a lift to reach high places safely, mixing durable pigment into paint built to resist sun, wind, and rain.

Painting a mural is rarely a one-person project. Large murals often require an entire team of artists who collaborate for days or even weeks. Sometimes community members, including students, help paint smaller sections under a lead artist's guidance. In Saudi cities such as Riyadh and Jeddah, mural projects have begun to brighten walls that were once blank and gray, turning quiet streets into vibrant landmarks.

versions.title: Street Art and Murals
versions.text:
A mural is a large-scale painting executed directly onto a wall, typically within an outdoor, public setting, and the individual who conceives and ultimately paints one is formally designated a muralist. Murals transform ordinary, frequently overlooked walls into vibrant works of public art that passersby can genuinely appreciate.

Murals appear on the sides of schools, shops, bridges, and apartment buildings across cities worldwide, often chosen specifically because they face busy thoroughfares where substantial numbers of people pass each day.

The word mural derives from an old Latin word, murus, meaning wall. People have decorated walls with pictures for thousands of years, but the large, public murals recognized today, often called street art, have become far more prevalent over recent decades. More municipalities began organizing mural festivals and inviting artists from abroad to collaborate with local talent, exchanging techniques and artistic styles along the way.

Before an artist can paint a large mural, a city or a building owner usually commissions the artist and offers a blank wall as a canvas. The surrounding community often suggests a theme, such as local history, nature, or a neighborhood story. The artist must obtain official permission from the relevant authority, since painting on a wall that belongs to someone else without authorization is legally considered vandalism, regardless of how talented the uninvited artist may be.

Turning a small sketch into a giant mural requires meticulous planning, since the design must be scaled up to the size of an entire building. Artists often draw a grid over their small design and a matching, much larger grid on the wall, so every square can be copied at the correct scale; some increasingly rely on design software to plan proportions precisely before projecting the outline onto the wall at night. For very tall walls, artists rely on scaffolding or a mechanical lift to reach high places safely, carefully mixing durable pigment into paint specifically formulated to resist sun, wind, and rain for many years without fading, cracking, or peeling.

Painting a mural is rarely a one-person project, since large murals often require an entire team of artists who collaborate closely for days or even weeks, acquiring new artistic skills along the way. In Saudi cities such as Riyadh and Jeddah, public art programs have begun to brighten walls that were once blank and gray, transforming quiet streets into vibrant landmarks that reinforce each city's distinct civic identity.

versions.title: Street Art and Murals
versions.text:
A mural is a large-scale painting executed directly onto a wall, typically within an outdoor, public setting, and the individual who conceives and ultimately paints one is formally designated a muralist, responsible for transforming an otherwise unremarkable surface into something extraordinary. Murals transform ordinary, frequently overlooked walls into vibrant works of public art that passersby can genuinely appreciate without ever stepping inside a museum or gallery.

Murals appear on the sides of schools, shops, bridges, and apartment buildings across cities worldwide, often chosen specifically because they face busy thoroughfares where substantial numbers of people pass each day, year after year.

The word mural derives from an old Latin word, murus, meaning wall, and people have decorated walls with pictures for thousands of years, but the large, public murals recognized today, often called street art, have become far more prevalent over recent decades, especially as municipalities increasingly began organizing mural festivals and inviting artists from abroad to collaborate extensively with local talent, exchanging techniques and artistic styles in the process.

Before an artist can paint a large mural, a city or a building owner usually commissions the artist and offers a blank wall as a canvas, while the surrounding community often suggests a theme, such as local history, nature, or a neighborhood story, and the artist must obtain official permission from the relevant authority, since painting on a wall that belongs to someone else without authorization is legally considered vandalism, regardless of how talented the uninvited artist may ultimately be.

Turning a small sketch into a giant mural requires meticulous, exacting planning, since the design must be scaled up precisely to the size of an entire building, and artists often draw a grid over their small design and a matching, much larger grid on the wall, so every square can be copied, section by section, at the correct scale, while some increasingly rely on specialized design software before projecting the outline onto the wall at night. For very tall walls, artists rely on scaffolding or a mechanical lift to reach high places safely, meticulously mixing durable pigment into paint specifically formulated to withstand sun, wind, and rain for many years without fading, cracking, or peeling.

Painting a mural is rarely ever a one-person project, since large murals often require an entire team of collaborating artists working closely together for days or even weeks, continuously acquiring new artistic skills along the way. In Saudi cities such as Riyadh and Jeddah, ambitious public art programs have begun to brighten walls that were once blank and gray, ultimately transforming quiet streets into vibrant landmarks that meaningfully reinforce each city's distinct civic identity.

keyWords.example: We will paint the fence white this weekend.

questions.stem: What is this article mostly about?

The history of Latin words
How murals are planned, painted, and brighten cities like Riyadh and Jeddah
How engineers carefully build very tall apartment buildings using steel and concrete beams
questions.why: The article explains what a mural is, how it gets planned and painted, and shows examples in Riyadh and Jeddah.

wrong.A: Mixing colors is only a small part of painting a mural.
wrong.B: The Latin word is mentioned only to explain where the name came from.
wrong.D: Building construction with steel is not discussed.

A small drawing on paper

HIGH.prompt: The article explains that creating a mural requires collaboration, careful planning, and official permission. Using evidence from the article, explain why each of these three elements is necessary, and describe how they work together to transform a blank wall into a landmark.
checklist: I explained why planning and permission matter.
I connected these ideas to how a mural becomes a landmark.
HIGH.modelAnswer: Collaboration matters because large murals often require an entire team of artists, and sometimes community volunteers, working together for days or weeks to finish such a big project. Careful planning matters because turning a small sketch into a giant mural requires a reliable method, such as a grid or projector, for scaling the design accurately onto a huge wall. Official permission matters because painting someone else's wall without asking is legally considered vandalism, no matter how skilled the artist is. Together, these three elements let a team transform a once-blank, gray wall into a vibrant landmark, like the mural projects that now brighten quiet streets in Riyadh and Jeddah.
